Meridian Health Systems Ltd
Corporate assurance pack for NHS procurements

This pack summarises the corporate, clinical safety, information governance and information security assurances that Meridian Health Systems Ltd provides to NHS buyers. It is maintained by the Bid Office and reviewed at each certificate renewal. The statements below are current as at 1 March 2025.

1. Clinical safety
Meridian Health Systems maintains a clinical safety case for the Meridian Care Record in accordance with DCB0129. The clinical safety case report was last reviewed on 14 January 2025 by our Clinical Safety Officer, Dr Amara Okafor, a registered nurse trained in clinical risk management. Hazards are recorded in a hazard log that is reviewed quarterly by the clinical safety group and shared with deploying organisations on request. We support each deploying organisation in meeting its own DCB0160 obligations by supplying the hazard log, the safety case report and a summary of residual risks before go-live.

2. Information governance
Meridian Health Systems Ltd (ODS code 8JX45) completed the Data Security and Protection Toolkit for 2024-25 with a status of Standards Met, published on 28 June 2025. Our Data Protection Officer is Priya Raman, who reports to the board quarterly. All patient data is processed in the United Kingdom under a data processing agreement aligned with the NHS England template.

3. Information security
Meridian Health Systems Ltd holds ISO 27001:2022 certification, certificate number IS 712345, issued by BSI on 4 March 2024 and valid until 3 March 2027. The scope covers the development, hosting and support of the Meridian Care Record. We also hold Cyber Essentials Plus, certificate number CEP-2025-118842, renewed on 1 February 2025 and expiring on 31 January 2026. Penetration tests are carried out annually by a CREST-accredited supplier.

4. Interoperability
The Meridian Care Record exposes FHIR R4 interfaces and is IM1 pairing integrated with EMIS Web and SystmOne. It supports GP Connect Access Record: HTML and structured record retrieval, and NHS login for patient-facing access. Messaging to acute trusts uses MESH.

5. Implementation and onboarding
A standard deployment runs over twelve weeks from contract signature to go-live, led by a named implementation manager. Training is delivered as a mix of on-site sessions and recorded modules, with a floor-walking presence for the first two weeks of live use. Clinical safety training is included for every customer super-user.
